Grout and flexible joints have different roles

Grout fills joints between tiles; silicone provides a flexible seal at suitable corners and changes of plane where movement needs to be accommodated. They are not interchangeable, and neither renews the concealed waterproofing membrane. We identify the joint type and check adjoining tiles before repair: filling a flexible junction with rigid grout does not provide the same movement allowance.

We assess the source first, then quote the suitable repair. Grout or silicone renewal may suit a joint problem; membrane renewal can require tile removal and coordinated retiling. Do you provide pool waterproofing as well as poolside tiling?

Pool surround or terrace tiling and pool-interior waterproofing are separate work areas. Any pool-interior scope is confirmed after assessment of the surfaces, suitable system and project requirements; poolside tile installation does not establish suitability for work inside the pool.
Is waterproofing required before tiling a wet area?

We install the specified wet-area waterproofing before the tiled finish, with surface preparation, drainage and junction details coordinated as part of the service. Tiles and grout alone do not provide the waterproofing layer.
How long does a waterproofing membrane last?

There is no single service-life figure for every membrane. The installed system, base condition, movement, exposure and use affect performance. We assess accessible surfaces and explain any investigation or renewal needed; intact tiles alone do not establish the condition beneath them.
Can waterproofing be done without removing tiles?

A local joint repair may be possible if assessment supports it. Regrouting or resealing does not replace a failed concealed membrane. We check the surface, joints and likely water-entry source, then identify any tile removal and membrane work in the written quote. The no-tile-removal explanation separates joint renewal from concealed membrane work.
Can you waterproof over existing tiles?

It depends on the selected system and the condition of the existing tiles and substrate. Waterproofing over tiles does not repair a failed concealed membrane. We inspect the area on site and specify any tile removal and preparation needed in the repair plan and written quote.
Do I need to replace the whole bathroom?

Not every shower leak needs a whole bathroom replacement. Assessment helps distinguish a joint problem, a plumbing source and affected waterproofing. We explain whether a targeted repair is suitable or which layers and finishes need removal and renewal.
What if the leak is already showing downstairs?

Avoid using the affected shower while the source is assessed. Tell us when the leak appears and which areas are affected. We arrange access to the relevant areas and identify the repair scope; plumbing or other trade assessment may also be needed before retiling.
Can you repair one damaged tile without replacing the whole floor?

We inspect the damaged tile and surrounding base before replacement. Matching tile availability, access and any underlying damage determine the scope. Your quote identifies the repair area and any preparation or waterproofing work needed.
What is included in tile regrouting and shower resealing?

Regrouting renews grout between tiles; resealing renews silicone at movement junctions and edges. We remove the deteriorated material, prepare the included joints and install suitable replacements. Neither process replaces a failed membrane, so recurring leaks need source assessment before the repair scope is agreed.
Can you tile over existing tiles?

Over-tiling may suit a sound, well-bonded base with acceptable flatness and finished height. We assess those conditions, edges and transitions before confirming the scope. Loose tiles or a failed concealed waterproofing layer need their own preparation or repair; another tile layer does not fix them.
Do you supply tiles or install tiles I have selected?

We install your selected tiles or include tile supply in the agreed scope. We confirm quantities, format, thickness and responsibility for materials before work begins. You can contact Ellis before choosing or buying tiles.
Why does floor flatness matter with large tiles?

Larger tiles can bridge variations in the base, affecting support, alignment and preparation. Flatness is different from making every floor level: the intended falls and complete floor build-up still matter. Our large-tile base preparation guidance explains what needs assessment before installation and quoting.
What should I check at floor tile height transitions?

Check the complete build-up at adjoining rooms, doors and appliances before installation. Tile thickness alone does not establish the finished height; preparation and installation layers affect the transition. See floor height transitions and connected-room layout for the details to check.
Should the benchtop be settled before splashback tiling?

The wall condition, final benchtop position and any replacement gaps need checking before setting the splashback layout. A movement junction needs a suitable flexible joint detail rather than being treated as an ordinary grout line. See wall and benchtop readiness before arranging the work.
How do I plan splashback cuts around outlets and a cooktop?

Plan the tile layout around outlets, exposed edges and the final benchtop, and confirm the selected materials are suitable for the appliance location. Clearances depend on the appliance instructions and applicable installation requirements. Plumbing and electrical changes need their own trade scope. Our splashback layout and material guidance explains the assessment points.
Does waterproofing go down before or after the screed?

There is no universal before-or-after rule. The specified waterproofing system determines whether the membrane sits above or below the screed or tile bed. Ellis confirms the project sequence before construction, coordinating drainage falls, junctions, finished tile height and the required waiting stages. Changing that sequence needs review of the complete system.
Can I keep the existing shower position?

It may be possible, depending on the layout, existing waste and drainage falls. We assess those details before membrane and tile installation. Any plumbing changes are a separate trade scope, with responsibilities and timing confirmed before the affected stages begin.
What if the existing waterproofing looks fine?

Appearance alone cannot confirm the concealed membrane's condition. We inspect the wet area, identify which layers the renovation will remove and explain the assessed renewal scope. If removal exposes extra substrate work, we obtain written approval before it proceeds.
What waterproofing and tiling services do you provide?

Ellis Services Group provides bathroom and wet-area waterproofing, wall and floor tiling, tile repairs, regrouting, shower resealing and pool surround tiling across Adelaide. How are waterproofing and tiling scheduled?

We coordinate preparation, the specified membrane stages, readiness checks, tiling and finishing. Surface dry, ready for the next coat, ready to tile and ready for use are different milestones. The selected product instructions and site conditions determine each waiting period, so a dry-looking surface is not permission to move to the next stage. When can I use the completed bathroom or tiled area?

Ready to tile does not mean the completed shower is ready for water or the floor is ready for traffic. Return to use also depends on the installed adhesive, grout and silicone, their product instructions and site conditions. We confirm likely downtime before work and provide project-specific handover instructions. Ask separately about walking on the area, normal use and water exposure; do not use touch-dry appearance as the deciding check. The return-to-use guide explains why appearance alone is not a readiness check.
What happens if additional damage is found during removal?
We explain the exposed condition and the additional work required, including its cost and timing. Extra work is confirmed with you in writing before it proceeds.
What do you provide at handover?

We explain the completed work and provide care and return-to-use instructions for the installed materials. Your written scope identifies the preparation, installation, checks and records agreed for the project. Ask about any applicable product and workmanship terms before booking; they are separate and depend on the agreed scope. Our handover and warranty questions help you clarify the job-specific records and terms.
What should I arrange for a rental or strata property?

Share the property location, affected room or surface, what you have observed and when it occurs. Provide the owner, property manager or strata contact, who can authorise work, and access arrangements for the affected and adjoining areas. Let us know about tenant appointments, keys, parking or building entry restrictions. Confirm authority before booking; our assessment describes the work and does not decide ownership boundaries, legal liability or who must pay.
